scenarios.name: QuickShip Checkout A/B Test
scenarios.summary: QuickShip is a fictional last-mile delivery company. Its product team ran an A/B test on a redesigned checkout button, comparing completion rates between the original (control) and redesigned (variation) button. Two versions of the test exist: a small pilot (50 users per group) and a full run (5,000 users per group), both showing a 10% lift. A data analyst must interpret sample size, p-values, confidence intervals, and statistical vs practical significance to advise whether to roll out the redesign company-wide.

scenarios.name: QuickShip Delivery Operations
scenarios.summary: QuickShip operates last-mile delivery across three Nigerian cities: Lagos, Abuja, and Kano. The operations team raised a complaint that deliveries feel slow. A data analyst scopes the question to: 'Which delivery zones are missing the delivery-time target, and by how much, over the last quarter?' Order records live in a SQL database (orders table: zone, driver_id, delivery_time_min, order_date); the driver roster is kept in an Excel workbook (driver_id, name, zone, shift). The analyst retrieves, cleans, models, analyzes, visualizes, and communicates findings to the Head of Operations, framing the Lagos slowdown as the priority finding and recommending adding one courier to the Lagos route.
glossary_example_vocab: Lagos delivery times rose to 30 minutes

assets.title: QuickShip Checkout A/B Test Results
assets.description: Summary table of A/B test runs for the QuickShip checkout-button redesign. Includes a small pilot (n=50 per group) and a large run (n=5000 per group), both showing the same 10% lift, plus two textbook proportion tests illustrating null-value-in-CI reasoning (null value 0.333).

assets.title: QuickShip City Delivery Summary
assets.description: City-level delivery performance summary for QuickShip's three operating cities. Lagos average delivery time rose to 30 minutes against a 25-minute target (primary finding). Kano also misses the target. Abuja is on target. Used to teach finding prioritization (Lagos slowdown is the primary finding) and actionable recommendation framing.

columns.name: target_min
columns.description: Company delivery-time target in minutes

columns.name: pct_on_time
columns.description: Percentage of deliveries meeting the target

columns.name: variability_rank
columns.description: Relative variability of delivery times: low or medium

columns.name: n_couriers
columns.description: Number of active couriers in this city

columns.name: finding_priority
columns.description: Priority of this city's finding for the operations manager: primary or secondary

assets.title: QuickShip Capstone Orders Table
assets.description: Last-quarter order records for QuickShip, retrieved via SQL query from the company's orders database. Columns match the glossary's capstone example: zone, driver_id, delivery_time_min, order_date. One row has a null delivery_time_min (missing value — a key data-quality teaching point). Covers four delivery zones: Lagos-North, Lagos-South, Kano-Central, Abuja-West.

assets.title: QuickShip Capstone Zone Delivery Summary
assets.description: Zone-level delivery performance summary produced by the capstone analysis. Answers the scoped question: which delivery zones are missing the 25-minute target, and by how much. Lagos-North and Lagos-South both miss the target; Abuja-West is fully on target. Used in the narrated stakeholder summary and deliverable documentation.
